restrictions: Messages are distinct 64-byte strings K || x and K || y for fixed prefix 0000008000000000000000800000000000000080000000000000000000000000; x and y are distinct little-endian 256-bit integers. The target uses the standard IV, counter 0, length 64, flags 11, 5 prefix rounds and all 256 output bits.
The walk is g(x)=f(x) XOR q for the fixed emitted polarity mask. One step has 30410 gates and uses 773 registers. This is a generic birthday search and claims no differential or weakness of BLAKE3.

The table is a seven-byte quotient filter with 116112 slots and capacity 116111: 36 stored key bits, 16 implied quotient bits, three filter bits, and a fixed 17-bit trail number. Word-aligned streams occupy 812800 bytes.
The exact operation total is 40353670902116666804367123481291840535235; division by C=1054 gives unrounded time_log2 124.848164562748. The submitted value is the next five-decimal upper endpoint.
The static image has 30441 native five-byte bitwise records, 1084 native five-byte recovery records, and 1335 36-byte controls, totaling 205685 bytes. No decoded compact instruction stream is used.
Search memory is 1048565 bytes and setup memory is 346661 bytes. Persistent counters and limits reside in the charged metadata region.

Recovery stores time-zero checkpoints, checks its cap before each call, snapshots packed outputs before input restoration, and rejects aliases, aligned starts, unequal endpoints, and equal predecessors.

One fresh uniform start is used with no amplification. Under H1, the stated lazy-sampled random-function program succeeds with probability at least 0.390000001002. H1 is score-critical; H3 is the supporting machine convention.

heuristics.statement: For the fixed 5-round walk and exact adaptive distinguished-point program, success is assumed to be at least the success probability of the same program with fresh evaluations answered by a lazy-sampled uniform random function on 256-bit values.
heuristics.scope: The fixed target on K || x, one run of 339151839689728000000000000000000000000 evaluations, and the stated halts, table, and recovery.
heuristics.extrapolation: The experiments execute the shipped program and compare a fixed width-20 restriction with calibrated shared random mappings. They do not observe the full 256-bit graph.
heuristics.limitations: H1 is a declared premise about one fixed function, not a theorem derived from the experiments.

heuristics.statement: The machine is a 256-bit load/store word RAM with 775 addressable registers, native five-byte register records, conservative 36-byte controls, and direct zero-test branches. Every code and data byte is charged.
heuristics.scope: The step, stage filter, handlers, quotient filter, recovery, setup, and runtime emitter.
heuristics.extrapolation: A machine without these declared encodings and registers requires separate accounting.
heuristics.limitations: H3 is an explicit machine convention rather than an organizer-fixed encoding.
